text: As a sequel to an accident which occurred at 2 p.m. yesterday at Prayu East, the driver of a hand truck was charged before Mr. S. B. B. McElderry at the Magistracy this morning with having no licence and driving recklessly.

label: text
text: Mr. N. M. Bux, giving evidence, stated that he was travelling in a riesha from east to west when he noticed a loaded hand truck come out from Landale Street at a fast pace and stand in the way of a trum car proceeding to Causeway Bay, the driver of the latter narrowly averting a collision by applying his emergency brake and pulling up with a jerk. The truck people then turned the truck round so suddenly that the shafts and one of the wheels of the riesha on which he was seated were smashed and the coolie slightly injured.

label: text
text: Sergeant Roberts said that the damage to the ricsha was estimated at $20, but he was not pressing for compensation as it was found that the coolie had been using a private ricsha for public hire.

label: text
text: The accused stated that in attempting to avoid a collision with the trum car he swerved the truck round and in doing so struck the riesha.

label: text
text: Fines amounting to $15 were imposed on the two counts.

label: text
text: A Chinese coolie in the employment of Drs. Dalmahoy Allan and Strahan was charged before Mr. S. B. B. McElderry at the Magistracy this morning with theft of money belonging to his employers.

label: text
text: Dr. Leslie Thomas informed His Worship that small sums of money mysteriously disappeared from time to time from the drawer of his table. It was discovered that the thefts took place between the time of closing the office in the evening and the following morning. On Monday evening he left some marked dollar notes in the drawer, which were found to be missing the next morning. The Police were informed, and Detective Sub-Inspector Dorling found one of the notes along with other money on searching the quarters of the accused.

label: text
text: The accused pleaded guilty and was sentenced to six weeks' hard labour.

label: text
text: A Chinese constable was brought before the Kowloon Magistrate this morning on a charge of neglecting his duty.

label: text
text: The accused had been sent out on his duty at midnight on Tuesday, and was reported to be asleep a few hours later at a small house in Cheung On Street. Sergeant McFadgean went to investigate and found the man sleeping in a canvas chair. The accused refused to open the door for the Sergeant, and the latter had to clamber through a window in effecting the arrest.

label: text
text: The accused, who had a bad record, was  $ ^{1} $sentenced "to pay a fine of 25 or undergo one month's hard labour.

label: text
text:
The payment to an employee by a client of a shop in Centre Street of an outstanding account amounting to $47.16 led to the appearance of that employee at the Central Magistracy yesterday.
The complainant was a partner in the firm and he charged the employee with theft of the money in question. The defendant did not deny that the money had been paid by the client and said that he had, in fact, told the complainant that it had been. It had not been paid to the complainant because there had been a quarrel among the partners of the firm in question and defendant had been told not to pay him money.
As the complainant admitted that the defendant had told him the money had been paid, His Worship (Mr. S. B. E. McElderry) said the action of the defendant was not like that of one guilty of larceny. The defendant was therefore discharged.

text: Four deaths from enteric fever have taken place during the week ending August 29, according to the return of the Medical Officer of Health. This and a further return for Monday show that five other people are down with enteric.

label: text
text: Of the total notifications, eight were reported from the Victoria district and one, from the New Territories. British cases numbered two, of which one was imported, Chinese five, Irish one and Portuguese one.

label: text
text: One British case of diphtheria and one Chinese case of paratyphoid fever have also been notified during the week and a death has also taken place from influenza.

label: text
text: The destroyer William Jones found one of the Hawaii bound seaplanes which had been forced to alight 300 miles from here.

label: text
text: The oil pipes of both engines were broken. The destroyer is towing the seaplane.

label: text
text: The seaplanes flying to Hawaii started off this afternoon. Flying conditions are almost perfect. —Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text: Though one seaplane travelling to Hawaii signalled her position as five hundred knots from here at 11.30 last night, the other machine has not reported for several hours. The guardship is searching for her.

label: text
text: The sub-committee appointed to draft the constitution of the proposed new alliance of railwaymen, transport workers, engineers and miners met in London to consider amendments to the proposed constitution submitted by the unions.

label: text
text: It is understood that these were numerous and that the National Union of Railwaymen took up a position indicating they would possibly be unable to support the alliance project as at present framed, contending that success was impossible until the unions of each industry composed their differences.

label: text
text: Fez, September 1. — Many tribes of Tsouls, Branes and Benizerouals continue to offer submission. They even offer troops to fight against Abd el Krim. Taking advantage of the later victories the French troops occupied the mountains near Dahar.—Havas.

label: text
text: Shanghai, September 1. — The whole party of kidnapped Church Missionary Society missionaries, who were kidnapped in Szechuan on August 6, were released on Sunday. All are well. Those kidnapped were—Bishop H. W. K. Mowll and his wife; the Reverend and Mrs. V. H. Donnithorne; Major F. W. Iles; Miss A. Settle; Miss M. Armfield and Miss C. Carleton.—Reuter.

text: Owing to the refusal of the demand for increased wages, the seamen employed by the Danish Sailing ship Owners Union struck. The Danish Unskilled Workers Union have declared a transport blockade against the owners affected.

label: text
text: Twenty-eight members of the committee of Red unions who were holding secret meetings in Bulcharest have been arrested.

label: text
text: They had announced an intensive propaganda campaign during the election of the labour councils.

text: Treasury officials announce that no Italian debt commission is expected to arrive on October 15.

label: text
text: With the Reich Railway Company's payment of interest on reparation bonds due yesterday, it is semi-officially claimed that Germany has completed the first year's payments under the Duves scheme.

label: text
text: The British steamer Theseus, from Batavia, had a fire in the forward part. A quantity of cargo was jettisoned. The vessel was not surveyed and proceeded on her way.

label: text
text: A message from Fez says news has been received of the sinking of the Spanish vessel "Espana-quinta" which was conveying troops to Alhucemas.

label: text
text: The Danish Foreign Minister and the Siamese Minister have signed a treaty of friendship, commerce and navigation based on the principles of reciprocity and the most favoured nation. The treaty must be ratified within six months.

label: text
text: Peking September 1.—It has been decided to start the so-called Christian College for those students of the five British missionary schools in Peking who do not desire to return thereto. Vernacular papers state that Feng Yu-hsiang has promised $10,000 to that end.—Reuter.
